headline: Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO; Nvidia falls 4.3 percent and gold sinks to 52-week low
subhead: S&P 500 slipped 0.4 percent to 7,592.4 as AMD rose 5.9 and Broadcom 5.5 percent, while gold fell 2.8 percent to 3,887.1 and bitcoin 4.2 percent.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to 7,592.4 and Nasdaq 0.4 percent to 25,366.1 after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO; Nvidia fell 4.3 percent.
Rotation into Nvidia rivals: AMD rose 5.9 percent and Broadcom 5.5 percent, while Strategy fell 6.5 percent on MSCI index removal.
Rates pressure: the 10-year yield reached about 5.1 percent and WTI rose 2.2 percent to 88.4 as Trump said no Iran deal is needed.

india.text: Nifty rose 0.8 percent to 25,255.1 and Bank Nifty 1.8 percent on 11 November, led by PSU banks and autos; Nifty closed at 25,299.35 on 12 November.
FIIs net bought Rs 7,830.6 crore and DIIs net sold Rs 6,331.2 crore on 12 November, per provisional data.
Rupee fell 33 paise to close at 94.04 per dollar on 12 November on a stronger greenback and a hawkish Fed tone.

global.text: Asia on 12 November: Hang Seng closed at 24,008.55 as Alibaba led a tech retreat; Alibaba ADRs fell 7.1 percent to a 52-week low.
Europe: the STOXX 600 hit a record high on 12 November on strong earnings, even as chip stocks fell on the Nvidia news.
Dollar index at a 52-week high of 103.2; gold fell 2.8 percent to a 52-week low of 3,887.1 and bitcoin 4.2 percent to 70,876.

weekly.narrative: The US midterms set the tone: a relief rally on Wednesday gave way to Thursday's AI chip rout on fears a Democratic Congress curbs data center building, and Friday's partial rebound and a 165,000 payrolls beat still left the S&P 500 down 2.7 percent and the Nasdaq 3.4 percent on the week. India went the other way, with foreign buying and cheaper crude lifting the Nifty 8.6 percent on the week and above 25,000 on Friday, while Kospi and the Nikkei bore the brunt of the chip selloff. Hopes of an Iran deal drove WTI down 12.8 percent on the week, and gold rose 4.5 percent and silver 5.5 percent despite rising Fed hike bets, while Bitcoin slipped 3.4 percent. Next week brings US CPI on 10 November, India CPI on 12 November, China's rare earth export pause expiring and a reported start to Anthropic's IPO roadshow.
